chapter: Arnold DePass's life and the Cadillac years
title: How her husband started drumming; Bechet and Joe Oliver
summary: He began beating sticks on his mother's bed; early band with Armstrong, Bechet unreliable, Joe Oliver, and her photograph of Oliver.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: I want to ask you how your husband got started, uh, playing drums.

Well, he started, uh, he told me he used to take two sticks, you know, drumsticks. And his mother had one of them wooden bits. And that's how he started beating drums on the back of the bed. And he used to say, I know, put them sticks down. His mother would get after him by putting the sticks down. And that's how he started playing drums. Beating on the back of his mother's bed. And then after that, well, when he started out with the drums, then he got the drums. That's when he was working with Parker Davis, when he got the drums. And then he got together. Louis Armstrong was in the home, I think. Yeah. Louis Armstrong was in the home, and they used to, now and then, René Clue was in there one time. And all that. Well, all of them used to come out, you know, and they, they was quite young, all children. And then they started up the band. And, uh, he had his brother with him. Day of the past, you know. And, uh, that's why I'll tell you, well, during that time, you'd get along, and they had, off and on, they'd have Bechet. Well, they had to bring him there and keep him there all day, you know. He was a very good fella and smart, but they really had to look him up because he wasn't reliable. And if you wanted to play a job tonight, well, you had to get him there and keep him all day. Because he'd blow you up. If somebody stopped him, he'd sure blow you up, you know. But he was a great musician. And, uh, and then also during that time, when they first started with the band, you had Joe Oliver. He was a yard boy, somewhere around Magazine and St. Mears. All even told me the people's names, but I forgot. And I heard something about Joe Oliver. Uh, when, uh, we was in the project. They was asking different people and we sent in to, uh, who was it? Uh, out there in the French Quarters. Oh, I can't get that fella's name. He had interviewed, uh, Lizzie Moran and, uh, he was talking about the history of, uh, of Joe Oliver and all them different bands. So I made my girl write a letter to the station that I had a picture of Joe Oliver and all that. And I would like to, like, get in touch with his wife and I would let her have it, you know, or something like that. But we never got the answer. We never got no answer for the picture. Because I didn't mind to say give him up, because maybe if I could get a little copy of him or something, just to have him. But I'd be glad to give him, almost, you know, all the information, you know. And he looks fine in there. He looks swell. That picture I have. I'm going to get it to show you. Yeah, Dr. Savings. And, uh, oh, so many of them boys all used to go along and they could pick him up somebody and make something out of him right away and put him in a band. I remember one time when the bands was hard to get. He sent some fellas out with them little, uh, with some other good mans that could play, uh, lead the band. He sent them out with a, how do you call that? A Zuzu? A Zuzu. Them little Zuzuz. He sent them out with them. That was one of them, then?
